Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS CloudTrail Lake: CloudTrail Lake queries API activity.
• AWS Artifact: Artifact provides compliance reports.
• Amazon Inspector: Inspector finds vulnerabilities.

Key takeaway: Find savings with Cost Explorer and Compute Optimizer.

stem: An analytics team runs occasional SQL queries on data in S3 and wants to pay only per query. Which approach is most cost-effective?

choices.text: An RDS instance loaded with the data every morning
A provisioned Redshift cluster running continuously
Amazon Athena on compressed, partitioned Parquet data
An EMR cluster running 24/7 for ad hoc queries

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Athena charges per data scanned; compressed, partitioned columnar data reduces scanned bytes.

Why the other options are wrong:
• An RDS instance loaded with the data every…: Daily loads into RDS are costly and slow.
• A provisioned Redshift cluster running…: Always-on clusters cost money when idle.
• An EMR cluster running 24/7 for ad hoc queries: Always-on EMR is costly.

Key takeaway: Pay-per-query on S3 → Athena with columnar data.

stem: A company's ECS services run on EC2 with low utilization. Which change can reduce cost and management?

choices.text: Use Dedicated Hosts for all of the container instances in the ECS cluster
Move services to Fargate or right-size and bin-pack with capacity providers
Add more EC2 instances to the cluster for extra headroom
Run each container on its own separate large EC2 instance

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Fargate removes idle instance capacity, and capacity providers with bin-packing improve utilization on EC2.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Use Dedicated Hosts for all of the container…: Dedicated Hosts cost more.
• Add more EC2 instances to the cluster for…: More instances increase cost.
• Run each container on its own separate large…: One container per large instance wastes capacity.

Key takeaway: Improve container cost with Fargate or better bin-packing.

stem: A company needs on-premises applications to use cloud storage for backups with local caching, minimizing on-premises hardware. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Storage Gateway
AWS Direct Connect
Amazon FSx for Lustre
Amazon EBS snapshots

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Storage Gateway provides on-premises access to cloud storage with local caching for backups and file shares.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS Direct Connect: Direct Connect is networking, not storage.
• Amazon FSx for Lustre: FSx for Lustre is for HPC in AWS.
• Amazon EBS snapshots: EBS snapshots are for EBS volumes.

Key takeaway: Hybrid storage with local cache → Storage Gateway.

stem: A company wants to track and alert on monthly spending per project. Which TWO steps help? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Use one account for all projects with no tags
Disable Cost Explorer to reduce reporting costs
Create AWS Budgets filtered by project tags
Remove tags from resources to simplify billing
Activate cost allocation tags for project tags

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Activated cost allocation tags enable project-level cost tracking, and Budgets alert on spending thresholds.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Use one account for all projects with no tags: No tags prevents tracking.
• Disable Cost Explorer to reduce reporting costs: Disabling Cost Explorer removes visibility.
• Remove tags from resources to simplify billing: Removing tags removes attribution.

Key takeaway: Track project costs with tags and budgets.

stem: A company wants to grant a contractor temporary access to one S3 bucket for two weeks without creating long-term credentials. Which approach fits?

choices.text: An IAM role the contractor can assume with a scoped policy and limited session duration
A bucket policy that allows public read and write access for the two weeks
The company administrator's credentials shared for the two-week project period
An IAM user with access keys that the contractor must promise to delete afterward

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Role assumption provides temporary credentials with scoped permissions.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A bucket policy that allows public read and…: Public access exposes data.
• The company administrator's credentials…: Sharing admin credentials is insecure.
• An IAM user with access keys that the…: Access keys are long-term credentials.

Key takeaway: Temporary access → assumable roles, not users or shared keys.

stem: A company wants to limit the maximum permissions developers can grant to the IAM roles they create. Which feature fits?

choices.text: VPC security group references
S3 bucket access control lists
AWS Budgets with alert actions
IAM permissions boundaries

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Permissions boundaries cap the maximum permissions an IAM entity can have.

Why the other options are wrong:
• VPC security group references: Security groups control network traffic.
• S3 bucket access control lists: ACLs control S3 object access.
• AWS Budgets with alert actions: Budgets control spending.

Key takeaway: Cap delegated permissions with permissions boundaries.

stem: An auditor asks which IAM users have unused access keys and when passwords were last changed. Which feature provides this quickly?

choices.text: The CloudFront usage report
The IAM credential report
The S3 inventory report
The Cost and Usage Report

explanation:
Why this is correct:
The credential report lists users and credential status, including key usage and password age.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The CloudFront usage report: CloudFront reports cover content delivery.
• The S3 inventory report: S3 inventory lists objects.
• The Cost and Usage Report: CUR covers billing.

Key takeaway: Credential status across users → IAM credential report.

stem: A policy allows s3:* on a bucket, but a user still gets Access Denied. The bucket belongs to another account. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: The user needs MFA only for console access, not for API calls
The S3 bucket is in a Region that the user's policy does not name
The bucket policy in the owning account does not grant the user access
The user's password has expired and must be reset in the console

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Cross-account access requires permission from both the caller's identity policy and the resource owner's bucket policy.

Why the other options are wrong:
• The user needs MFA only for console access,…: MFA is not implied as the cause.
• The S3 bucket is in a Region that the user's…: S3 permissions do not require naming Regions.
• The user's password has expired and must be…: Password expiry affects console sign-in, not API permissions here.

Key takeaway: Cross-account access needs both identity and resource policy grants.

stem: An application tier must be reachable only from the web tier, and the database only from the application tier. Which design fits?

choices.text: Public subnets for all tiers with security groups open to 0.0.0.0/0
Network ACLs that allow all traffic within the whole VPC CIDR range
One security group shared by all tiers that allows all inbound traffic
Separate security groups per tier, each allowing traffic only from the tier in front

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Chained security groups restrict each tier to traffic from the previous tier.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Public subnets for all tiers with security…: Public exposure is insecure.
• Network ACLs that allow all traffic within…: Allowing all VPC traffic removes isolation.
• One security group shared by all tiers that…: One open group removes isolation.

Key takeaway: Chain security groups tier by tier.

stem: A company wants to block traffic from a set of malicious IP addresses to all public subnets quickly. Security groups allow only permit rules. Which control fits?

choices.text: Network ACL deny rules on the public subnets
A security group rule with a deny statement
An IAM policy denying the IP addresses
A Route 53 record pointing to a blackhole

explanation:
Why this is correct:
NACLs support explicit deny rules at the subnet level.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A security group rule with a deny statement: Security groups cannot deny.
• An IAM policy denying the IP addresses: IAM policies do not filter network traffic.
• A Route 53 record pointing to a blackhole: DNS records do not block inbound traffic.

Key takeaway: Explicit network denies → NACLs.

stem: A company wants to inspect and filter traffic leaving its VPC to the internet, allowing only approved domains. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon GuardDuty with default settings
AWS Network Firewall with domain allow lists
Security groups with outbound rules by IP
An internet gateway with a route table only

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Network Firewall supports stateful domain filtering for egress traffic.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon GuardDuty with default settings: GuardDuty detects threats but does not filter traffic.
• Security groups with outbound rules by IP: Security groups filter by IP and port, not domain.
• An internet gateway with a route table only: IGWs route but do not filter.

Key takeaway: Domain-based egress filtering → Network Firewall.

stem: Applications in a VPC must access an internal service in another VPC with an overlapping CIDR. Which option fits?

choices.text: A transit gateway with one route table
VPC peering between the two VPCs
Public internet with IP allow lists
AWS PrivateLink with an endpoint service

explanation:
Why this is correct:
PrivateLink exposes a specific service without routing between VPCs, so overlapping CIDRs are not a problem.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A transit gateway with one route table: Overlapping routes conflict.
• VPC peering between the two VPCs: Peering fails with overlapping CIDRs.
• Public internet with IP allow lists: Public routing is less secure.

Key takeaway: Overlapping CIDRs and one service → PrivateLink.

stem: A company wants continuous threat detection that analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Artifact
Amazon GuardDuty
Amazon Inspector
AWS Firewall Manager

explanation:
Why this is correct:
GuardDuty analyzes these data sources to detect threats continuously.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS Artifact: Artifact provides compliance documents.
• Amazon Inspector: Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.
• AWS Firewall Manager: Firewall Manager manages firewall rules.

Key takeaway: Continuous threat detection → GuardDuty.

stem: A company must rotate RDS database credentials automatically and let applications retrieve them securely. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Secrets Manager
AWS Certificate Manager
Amazon Cognito user pools
AWS Resource Access Manager

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Secrets Manager stores and rotates credentials, including native rotation for RDS.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS Certificate Manager: ACM manages TLS certificates.
• Amazon Cognito user pools: Cognito manages app users.
• AWS Resource Access Manager: RAM shares resources.

Key takeaway: Rotating database credentials → Secrets Manager.

stem: A company needs keys stored in single-tenant hardware security modules it controls, for regulatory reasons. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS KMS keys
AWS Secrets Manager
AWS CloudHSM
Amazon Macie

explanation:
Why this is correct:
CloudHSM provides dedicated HSMs under the customer's exclusive control.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS KMS keys: Standard KMS keys use multi-tenant HSMs managed by AWS.
• AWS Secrets Manager: Secrets Manager stores secrets.
• Amazon Macie: Macie discovers sensitive data.

Key takeaway: Dedicated HSM control → CloudHSM.

stem: A company requires that all new EBS volumes in an account are encrypted automatically. What should be done?

choices.text: Enable EBS encryption by default in each Region
Ask engineers to select encryption when creating volumes
Use instance store volumes for all workloads
Enable encryption on existing snapshots only

explanation:
Why this is correct:
EBS encryption by default encrypts all new volumes in that Region.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Ask engineers to select encryption when…: Manual selection is error-prone.
• Use instance store volumes for all workloads: Instance store is ephemeral.
• Enable encryption on existing snapshots only: Snapshots do not change new volume defaults.

Key takeaway: Enforce EBS encryption by default.

stem: Data in an S3 bucket must be accessible only through a specific VPC endpoint. Which control enforces this?

choices.text: A NACL on the subnet denying access to all S3 IPs
An IAM user policy denying access from outside the office
A bucket policy denying requests where aws:SourceVpce is not the endpoint
A security group on the bucket allowing only the VPC CIDR

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Bucket policies with the aws:SourceVpce condition restrict access to a specific VPC endpoint.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A NACL on the subnet denying access to all…: NACLs cannot reliably target S3.
• An IAM user policy denying access from…: User policies do not cover all principals or the network path.
• A security group on the bucket allowing only…: Buckets do not have security groups.

Key takeaway: Lock S3 to a VPC endpoint with bucket policy conditions.

stem: A company wants to prevent objects in an S3 bucket from being made public by ACLs. Which setting fits?

choices.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering setting
S3 Block Public Access settings
S3 Requester Pays setting
S3 Transfer Acceleration setting

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Block Public Access overrides ACLs and policies that would grant public access.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 Intelligent-Tiering setting: Intelligent-Tiering optimizes cost.
• S3 Requester Pays setting: Requester Pays shifts request costs.
• S3 Transfer Acceleration setting: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads.

Key takeaway: Prevent public S3 access with Block Public Access.

stem: Which TWO practices follow the principle of least privilege? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Share one IAM user among the whole team
Use the root user for daily administrative tasks
Give all developers AdministratorAccess by default
Grant only the permissions required for each task
Review and remove unused permissions regularly

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Least privilege means granting only needed permissions and pruning unused ones.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Share one IAM user among the whole team: Shared users remove accountability.
• Use the root user for daily administrative tasks: Root should not be used daily.
• Give all developers AdministratorAccess by…: Admin access for all violates least privilege.

Key takeaway: Grant minimal permissions and prune regularly.

stem: Which TWO services help protect a public web application at the edge? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Amazon EBS
Amazon RDS
AWS Batch
Amazon CloudFront
AWS WAF

explanation:
Why this is correct:
CloudFront absorbs traffic at the edge, and WAF filters malicious requests.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon EBS: EBS is block storage.
• Amazon RDS: RDS is a database.
• AWS Batch: Batch runs batch jobs.

Key takeaway: Edge protection → CloudFront plus WAF.

stem: Which TWO options encrypt data at rest in Amazon S3? (Select TWO)

choices.text: SSE-S3 with S3 managed keys
VPC endpoints for S3
S3 Transfer Acceleration
TLS on client connections
SSE-KMS with KMS keys

explanation:
Why this is correct:
SSE-S3 and SSE-KMS encrypt objects at rest.

Why the other options are wrong:
• VPC endpoints for S3: Endpoints provide private network paths.
• S3 Transfer Acceleration: Acceleration speeds transfers.
• TLS on client connections: TLS encrypts in transit.

Key takeaway: At-rest S3 encryption → SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS.

stem: A company wants a central view of security findings and compliance checks across its accounts. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Security Hub
AWS DataSync
Amazon CloudFront

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Security Hub aggregates findings and runs security standard checks across accounts.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS Cost Explorer: Cost Explorer analyzes spending.
• AWS DataSync: DataSync transfers data.
• Amazon CloudFront: CloudFront is a CDN.

Key takeaway: Centralized security posture → Security Hub.

stem: A company needs employees to access a private web application in a VPC without a VPN, with identity-based access checks for each request. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Direct Connect
AWS Global Accelerator
AWS Verified Access
Amazon Route 53

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Verified Access provides VPN-less, identity- and device-aware access to private applications.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS Direct Connect: Direct Connect is private connectivity from data centers.
• AWS Global Accelerator: Global Accelerator improves routing, not access control.
• Amazon Route 53: Route 53 is DNS.

Key takeaway: VPN-less zero-trust app access → Verified Access.

stem: A company must keep a record of every configuration change to its security groups for audits. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Glue
AWS Config
Amazon Polly
Amazon SQS

explanation:
Why this is correct:
AWS Config records configuration history and changes for resources such as security groups.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS Glue: Glue integrates data.
• Amazon Polly: Polly synthesizes speech.
• Amazon SQS: SQS queues messages.

Key takeaway: Configuration history → AWS Config.

stem: A company wants to detect IAM roles and S3 buckets that are shared with external accounts. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon Detective
AWS Trusted Advisor
IAM Access Analyzer
AWS Batch

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Access Analyzer identifies resources shared with principals outside the zone of trust.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon Detective: Detective investigates findings.
• AWS Trusted Advisor: Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks.
• AWS Batch: Batch runs jobs.

Key takeaway: External sharing detection → Access Analyzer.

stem: An application uses a third-party appliance to inspect traffic and must scale it transparently. Which load balancer fits?

choices.text: Gateway Load Balancer
Application Load Balancer
Network Load Balancer
Classic Load Balancer

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Gateway Load Balancer deploys, scales, and manages third-party virtual appliances transparently.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Application Load Balancer: ALB is for HTTP applications.
• Network Load Balancer: NLB is for TCP/UDP applications.
• Classic Load Balancer: Classic is legacy.

Key takeaway: Scale inspection appliances with Gateway Load Balancer.

stem: A web application stores user sessions in instance memory, so users are logged out when instances are replaced. Which change fixes this?

choices.text: Enable sticky sessions with no expiration
Use one large instance instead of many
Disable Auto Scaling for the application
Store sessions in ElastiCache or DynamoDB

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Externalizing session state lets any instance serve any user and survives instance replacement.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Enable sticky sessions with no expiration: Sticky sessions still lose state on replacement.
• Use one large instance instead of many: One instance is a single point of failure.
• Disable Auto Scaling for the application: Disabling scaling hurts availability.

Key takeaway: Make web tiers stateless.

stem: A company wants to route events from AWS services and SaaS applications to different targets based on event content. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon EventBridge
Amazon Kinesis
Amazon SQS FIFO
AWS Batch jobs

explanation:
Why this is correct:
EventBridge routes events from AWS services and SaaS partners to targets using content-based rules.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon Kinesis: Kinesis streams data for consumers to process.
• Amazon SQS FIFO: SQS queues messages without content routing rules.
• AWS Batch jobs: Batch runs jobs.

Key takeaway: Content-based event routing → EventBridge.

stem: A queue's consumers process messages slowly during spikes, and the backlog grows. Which change helps most?

choices.text: Reduce the message retention period to one minute
Increase the maximum message size to 2 GB
Scale consumers with Auto Scaling based on queue depth
Delete messages that wait longer than a second

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Scaling consumers on queue depth adds capacity when the backlog grows.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Reduce the message retention period to one…: Short retention loses messages.
• Increase the maximum message size to 2 GB: Message size does not speed processing.
• Delete messages that wait longer than a second: Deleting messages loses data.

Key takeaway: Scale consumers on backlog.

stem: Messages that repeatedly fail processing block a queue. Which feature isolates them?

choices.text: A larger batch size for each receive call
A dead-letter queue with a max receive count
A shorter polling interval for consumers
A longer visibility timeout of twelve hours

explanation:
Why this is correct:
A DLQ moves messages that fail too many times, so processing continues.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A larger batch size for each receive call: Batch size does not isolate failures.
• A shorter polling interval for consumers: Polling interval does not isolate failures.
• A longer visibility timeout of twelve hours: Longer visibility delays retries but does not remove failing messages.

Key takeaway: Isolate failing messages with DLQs.

stem: A company wants to test how its application responds to an EC2 instance failure in a controlled way. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Trusted Advisor checks
Amazon Inspector
AWS Config rules
AWS Fault Injection Service

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Fault Injection Service runs controlled experiments such as stopping instances to test resilience.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS Trusted Advisor checks: Trusted Advisor gives recommendations.
• Amazon Inspector: Inspector finds vulnerabilities.
• AWS Config rules: Config evaluates configurations.

Key takeaway: Test resilience with fault injection.

stem: A global application needs a relational database that serves low-latency reads in multiple Regions and can fail over to another Region quickly. Which option fits?

choices.text: DynamoDB global tables
RDS Multi-AZ in one Region
Amazon Aurora Global Database
RDS snapshots copied weekly

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Aurora Global Database replicates to secondary Regions for local reads and fast Regional failover.

Why the other options are wrong:
• DynamoDB global tables: DynamoDB is not relational.
• RDS Multi-AZ in one Region: Multi-AZ stays within one Region.
• RDS snapshots copied weekly: Weekly snapshots are too slow.

Key takeaway: Multi-Region relational reads and DR → Aurora Global Database.

stem: An application must keep serving users if one of three Availability Zones fails, with no reduction in capacity. How should capacity be planned?

choices.text: Provision enough capacity so the remaining two AZs can handle full load
Place all instances in the AZ with the most available capacity
Provision exactly the capacity needed with all AZs working normally
Rely on Auto Scaling in a single AZ to replace failed instances

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Static stability means running enough spare capacity so losing one AZ does not reduce service.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Place all instances in the AZ with the most…: Single-AZ placement fails with the AZ.
• Provision exactly the capacity needed with…: Losing an AZ would reduce capacity.
• Rely on Auto Scaling in a single AZ to…: Single-AZ scaling does not survive AZ loss.

Key takeaway: Plan capacity for the loss of one AZ.

stem: Which TWO features protect S3 data against accidental deletion? (Select TWO)

choices.text: S3 Storage Lens
S3 Transfer Acceleration
S3 Select queries
MFA Delete
S3 Versioning

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Versioning keeps prior versions, and MFA Delete requires MFA to permanently delete versions.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 Storage Lens: Storage Lens reports usage.
• S3 Transfer Acceleration: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads.
• S3 Select queries: S3 Select queries objects.

Key takeaway: Protect S3 data with versioning and MFA Delete.

stem: A company needs to run containers on Kubernetes with AWS managing the control plane. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon EMR
Amazon EKS
AWS Batch
Amazon ECS

explanation:
Why this is correct:
EKS provides a managed Kubernetes control plane.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon EMR: EMR runs big data frameworks.
• AWS Batch: Batch runs batch jobs.
• Amazon ECS: ECS is AWS's own orchestrator, not Kubernetes.

Key takeaway: Managed Kubernetes → EKS.

stem: A company must recover an EC2-based application in another Region within hours at the lowest cost. Which strategy fits?

choices.text: Multi-site active-active at full production capacity in both Regions
Warm standby at full production scale in the other Region
Backup and restore with AMIs and snapshots copied to the other Region
Pilot light with all servers running in the other Region

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Backup and restore is the cheapest approach and fits recovery within hours.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Multi-site active-active at full production…: Active-active is the most expensive.
• Warm standby at full production scale in the…: Full-scale warm standby is costly.
• Pilot light with all servers running in the…: Running all servers is not pilot light and costs more.

Key takeaway: Hours of RTO at lowest cost → backup and restore.

stem: Which TWO options help an application absorb sudden traffic spikes without dropping requests? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Remove the load balancer to reduce overhead
Buffer requests in an SQS queue
Hard-code a maximum of one worker instance
Disable retries in the client applications
Use Auto Scaling for the processing tier

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Queues buffer bursts, and Auto Scaling adds capacity to work through them.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Remove the load balancer to reduce overhead: Removing the load balancer reduces availability.
• Hard-code a maximum of one worker instance: One worker cannot absorb spikes.
• Disable retries in the client applications: Disabling retries drops requests.

Key takeaway: Buffer and scale to absorb spikes.

stem: A company wants its Lambda-based API to keep working if a single Availability Zone fails. What is required?

choices.text: Nothing extra, since Lambda runs across multiple AZs by default
Configure a NAT gateway in a single Availability Zone for all of the functions
Attach an Elastic IP address to each function
Deploy a copy of each function manually in every AZ

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Lambda runs functions across multiple AZs in a Region automatically.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Configure a NAT gateway in a single…: A single-AZ NAT gateway would add an AZ dependency for VPC-attached functions.
• Attach an Elastic IP address to each function: Functions do not use Elastic IPs.
• Deploy a copy of each function manually in…: Functions are not deployed per AZ.

Key takeaway: Lambda is multi-AZ by default.

stem: A company uses one EC2 instance as a NAT for private subnets. Which change improves resilience with minimal management?

choices.text: Remove NAT entirely and use public IPs everywhere
Add a second NAT instance with no route changes
Replace it with a larger NAT instance in the same AZ
Replace it with NAT gateways in each Availability Zone

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Managed NAT gateways in each AZ remove the single point of failure and maintenance burden.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Remove NAT entirely and use public IPs…: Public IPs expose instances.
• Add a second NAT instance with no route changes: Without route changes, the second instance is unused.
• Replace it with a larger NAT instance in the…: A larger instance is still a single point of failure.

Key takeaway: Use managed NAT gateways per AZ.

stem: A company wants a managed message broker compatible with existing RabbitMQ clients. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon SQS
Amazon SNS
Amazon MQ
Amazon MSK

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Amazon MQ provides managed ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ brokers compatible with existing clients.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon SQS: SQS uses its own API.
• Amazon SNS: SNS uses its own API.
• Amazon MSK: MSK is managed Kafka.

Key takeaway: Managed RabbitMQ or ActiveMQ → Amazon MQ.

stem: An application writes files to an EC2 instance store volume and loses them when the instance stops. Which change keeps the data?

choices.text: Use a larger instance type with more storage
Increase the size of the instance store volume
Enable detailed monitoring on the instance
Store the files on EBS, EFS, or S3 instead

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Instance store is ephemeral; persistent storage such as EBS, EFS, or S3 keeps data.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Use a larger instance type with more storage: Larger instance store is still ephemeral.
• Increase the size of the instance store volume: Size does not make it persistent.
• Enable detailed monitoring on the instance: Monitoring does not preserve data.

Key takeaway: Use persistent storage for data that must survive stops.

stem: A company wants DNS health checks to route traffic only to healthy endpoints and return multiple healthy IP addresses to clients. Which routing policy fits?

choices.text: Latency routing only
Multivalue answer routing
Geolocation routing
Simple routing policy records

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Multivalue answer routing returns several healthy records, each with health checks.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Latency routing only: Latency routing returns the lowest-latency record.
• Geolocation routing: Geolocation routes by location.
• Simple routing policy records: Simple routing has no health checks.

Key takeaway: Multiple healthy IPs from DNS → multivalue answer routing.

stem: A company processes large batch jobs that require hundreds of instances and job queues with dependencies. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Batch
Amazon SQS
Amazon SNS
AWS Lambda

explanation:
Why this is correct:
AWS Batch manages job queues and provisions compute for large batch workloads.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon SQS: SQS queues messages but does not manage compute.
• Amazon SNS: SNS publishes notifications.
• AWS Lambda: Lambda has time limits for long batch jobs.

Key takeaway: Large managed batch processing → AWS Batch.

stem: A company wants recovery points for EBS volumes every hour with automatic cleanup after seven days. Which feature fits?

choices.text: Manual snapshots created each hour by the operations team
EC2 instance store backups with cron jobs
S3 lifecycle rules applied to the EBS volumes
Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager or AWS Backup policies

explanation:
Why this is correct:
DLM and AWS Backup automate snapshot creation and retention.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Manual snapshots created each hour by the…: Manual snapshots are error-prone.
• EC2 instance store backups with cron jobs: Instance store is ephemeral.
• S3 lifecycle rules applied to the EBS volumes: S3 lifecycle rules do not apply to EBS volumes.

Key takeaway: Automate EBS snapshot schedules and retention.

stem: A company wants to decouple a monolith gradually by extracting features into microservices behind a single API entry point. Which service helps route requests?

choices.text: AWS DataSync jobs
AWS Snowball Edge
Amazon API Gateway
Amazon S3 buckets

explanation:
Why this is correct:
API Gateway can route specific paths to new services while others still go to the monolith.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS DataSync jobs: DataSync transfers files.
• AWS Snowball Edge: Snowball moves data offline.
• Amazon S3 buckets: S3 stores objects.

Key takeaway: Route requests during decomposition with API Gateway.

stem: A workload needs low-latency file storage for Windows applications with SMB and Active Directory integration. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon S3 Standard storage class
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
Amazon EBS gp3 volume on one host
Amazon EFS Standard storage class

explanation:
Why this is correct:
FSx for Windows File Server provides SMB shares with AD integration.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon S3 Standard storage class: S3 is object storage.
• Amazon EBS gp3 volume on one host: An EBS volume is not a shared file system.
• Amazon EFS Standard storage class: EFS uses NFS for Linux.

Key takeaway: Windows file shares → FSx for Windows File Server.

stem: An application needs single-digit millisecond access to frequently accessed S3 data in one Availability Zone with the highest request rates. Which storage class fits?

choices.text: S3 Express One Zone
S3 One Zone-IA
S3 Glacier Instant
S3 Standard-IA

explanation:
Why this is correct:
S3 Express One Zone provides very low latency and high request rates for frequently accessed data in one AZ.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 One Zone-IA: One Zone-IA is for infrequent access.
• S3 Glacier Instant: Glacier Instant Retrieval is for rarely accessed data.
• S3 Standard-IA: Standard-IA is for infrequent access.

Key takeaway: Ultra-low-latency, high-rate S3 access → S3 Express One Zone.

stem: A machine learning training job needs GPU acceleration. Which EC2 instance category fits?

choices.text: Accelerated computing instances such as P or G families
Burstable instances such as the T family
Storage optimized instances such as the I or D families
Memory optimized instances such as X family

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Accelerated computing instances provide GPUs for ML training and graphics.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Burstable instances such as the T family: Burstable instances lack GPUs.
• Storage optimized instances such as the I or…: Storage optimized targets local I/O.
• Memory optimized instances such as X family: Memory optimized targets RAM, not GPUs.

Key takeaway: GPU workloads → accelerated computing instances.

stem: A company wants EC2 instances with the best price-performance for general Linux workloads. Which option often fits?

choices.text: Bare metal instances for all apps
AWS Graviton-based instances
Previous-generation instance types
Dedicated Hosts for every workload

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Graviton-based instances offer strong price-performance for many Linux workloads.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Bare metal instances for all apps: Bare metal is for special needs.
• Previous-generation instance types: Older generations usually have worse price-performance.
• Dedicated Hosts for every workload: Dedicated Hosts cost more.

Key takeaway: Improve price-performance with Graviton instances.

stem: A DynamoDB table receives repeated reads for the same items and needs microsecond latency. Which feature fits?

choices.text: DynamoDB Streams
DynamoDB global tables replication
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)
DynamoDB TTL

explanation:
Why this is correct:
DAX is an in-memory cache for DynamoDB that delivers microsecond read latency.

Why the other options are wrong:
• DynamoDB Streams: Streams capture changes.
• DynamoDB global tables replication: Global tables replicate across Regions.
• DynamoDB TTL: TTL expires items.

Key takeaway: Microsecond DynamoDB reads → DAX.

stem: Which TWO actions reduce read latency for an RDS-backed application? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Reduce the instance size to save cost
Increase the backup retention period
Enable Multi-AZ to use the standby for reads
Cache frequent query results in ElastiCache
Add read replicas for read-heavy queries

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Read replicas offload reads, and caching serves repeated queries from memory.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Reduce the instance size to save cost: Smaller instances increase latency.
• Increase the backup retention period: Retention does not affect latency.
• Enable Multi-AZ to use the standby for reads: The Multi-AZ instance standby does not serve reads.

Key takeaway: Offload and cache reads.

stem: A company needs consistent network performance and private connectivity between its data center and AWS for large transfers. Which option fits?

choices.text: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
Internet gateway
VPC peering
AWS Direct Connect

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Direct Connect provides dedicated private connectivity with consistent performance.

Why the other options are wrong:
• AWS Site-to-Site VPN: VPN runs over the internet with variable performance.
• Internet gateway: IGWs provide internet access.
• VPC peering: Peering connects VPCs.

Key takeaway: Consistent private hybrid bandwidth → Direct Connect.

stem: Instances in a placement group need the lowest network latency for tightly coupled HPC. Which placement strategy fits?

choices.text: No placement group at all
Cluster placement group
Spread placement group
Partition placement group

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Cluster placement groups place instances close together for low latency and high throughput.

Why the other options are wrong:
• No placement group at all: Default placement does not optimize latency.
• Spread placement group: Spread groups separate instances for resilience.
• Partition placement group: Partition groups separate groups of instances for large distributed systems.

Key takeaway: Low-latency HPC → cluster placement group.

stem: A company wants to transform data in S3 with serverless ETL jobs and a central data catalog. Which service fits?

choices.text: AWS Glue
Amazon RDS
AWS Outposts
Amazon EBS

explanation:
Why this is correct:
AWS Glue provides serverless ETL and a Data Catalog.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon RDS: RDS is a database.
• AWS Outposts: Outposts extends AWS on premises.
• Amazon EBS: EBS is block storage.

Key takeaway: Serverless ETL and catalog → AWS Glue.

stem: Business users need interactive dashboards on data in Athena and Redshift. Which service fits?

choices.text: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon SQS
Amazon Quick Sight
AWS Glue jobs

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Quick Sight provides BI dashboards on data sources such as Athena and Redshift.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: Kinesis streams data.
• Amazon SQS: SQS queues messages.
• AWS Glue jobs: Glue transforms data.

Key takeaway: BI dashboards → Quick Sight.

stem: A company needs to move 80 TB of data to AWS within a week over a slow internet link. Which option fits?

choices.text: A Site-to-Site VPN upload
S3 Transfer Acceleration
AWS DataSync over the internet
AWS Snowball Edge devices

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Snowball devices move large data volumes offline faster than slow network links allow.

Why the other options are wrong:
• A Site-to-Site VPN upload: VPN is limited by the link.
• S3 Transfer Acceleration: Transfer Acceleration is still limited by bandwidth.
• AWS DataSync over the internet: DataSync is limited by bandwidth.

Key takeaway: Large transfers over slow links → Snowball.

stem: An application needs to store and serve user-uploaded images at any scale with high durability. Which service fits?

choices.text: Instance store
Amazon S3
Amazon EBS
Amazon EFS One Zone

explanation:
Why this is correct:
S3 provides highly durable, scalable object storage for images.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Instance store: Instance store is ephemeral.
• Amazon EBS: EBS attaches to one instance.
• Amazon EFS One Zone: EFS One Zone has lower durability and higher cost per GB for this use.

Key takeaway: Durable, scalable object storage → S3.

stem: A containerized web service needs to scale tasks automatically based on CPU. Which feature fits?

choices.text: Manual task starts by the operations team
A scheduled Lambda that adds one task daily
ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking
A fixed desired count set once at launch

explanation:
Why this is correct:
ECS Service Auto Scaling adjusts task count based on metrics such as CPU.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Manual task starts by the operations team: Manual scaling is slow.
• A scheduled Lambda that adds one task daily: Daily additions do not track load.
• A fixed desired count set once at launch: A fixed count cannot follow load.

Key takeaway: Scale containers with Service Auto Scaling.

stem: Backups must be kept for ten years and are almost never retrieved; retrieval within 48 hours is acceptable. Which storage class is cheapest?

choices.text: S3 Glacier Deep Archive
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Standard-IA
S3 Intelligent-Tiering

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class for rarely accessed data with retrieval in hours.

Why the other options are wrong:
• S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval: Instant Retrieval costs more for data almost never retrieved.
• S3 Standard-IA: Standard-IA costs more.
• S3 Intelligent-Tiering: Intelligent-Tiering adds monitoring costs and is not as cheap for archival.

Key takeaway: Long-term archives → Glacier Deep Archive.

stem: A company runs a steady fleet of the same EC2 instance family in one Region for three years and wants the largest discount. Which option fits?

choices.text: EC2 Instance Savings Plans or Standard Reserved Instances
Spot Instances for all steady production workloads
Dedicated Hosts purchased on demand for each instance
On-Demand instances with detailed monitoring

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Instance-family commitments provide the largest discounts for steady, predictable usage.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Spot Instances for all steady production…: Spot can be interrupted.
• Dedicated Hosts purchased on demand for each…: Dedicated Hosts cost more.
• On-Demand instances with detailed monitoring: On-Demand costs more.

Key takeaway: Steady, fixed-family usage → Instance Savings Plans or Standard RIs.

stem: A company has variable workloads and wants to combine Spot and On-Demand capacity in one Auto Scaling group. Which feature fits?

choices.text: Manual scaling with On-Demand only
A mixed instances policy with capacity rebalancing
A single instance type with Spot only
A launch template that uses Dedicated Hosts only

explanation:
Why this is correct:
Mixed instances policies combine purchase options and instance types, and capacity rebalancing reduces Spot interruptions.

Why the other options are wrong:
• Manual scaling with On-Demand only: Manual On-Demand scaling is costly and slow.
• A single instance type with Spot only: A single Spot type risks interruptions.
• A launch template that uses Dedicated Hosts only: Dedicated Hosts are costly.

Key takeaway: Blend Spot and On-Demand with mixed instances policies.

stem: A read-only reporting database copy is needed only for monthly reports. Which approach minimizes cost?

choices.text: Buy a three-year reserved instance for the monthly reporting copy
Run Multi-AZ for the reporting copy at all times
Keep a large read replica running all month long
